title: r
text: The r subcommand is used to set up R environments.

title: r
text:
Commands
  r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr]

title: r
text:
Setup
One may often use a non-standard R terminal named radian because it offers many enhancements over the standard R terminal. However, radian (in some experiences) breaks without a key configuration setting.
To configure this setting, run the following command:
setupmjr r
In addition to configuring radian, this command also turns off object length and line linters for lintr (to prevent VS Code or other editors from bothering you because your variable names or lines are “too long”).

Flags
You can opt out of configuring radian or lintr by passing the respective flags:

--not-radian: Do not configure ~/.radian_profile.
--not-lintr: Do not configure ~/.lintr.

For example, to only configure radian and not lintr:
setupmjr r --not-lintr

title: r
text:
Details
If not skipped via --not-radian, the ~/.radian_profile file is created if it does not exist, and the following line is added to it:
options(radian.auto_match = FALSE)
If not skipped via --not-lintr, the ~/.lintr file is created if it does not exist, and the following lines are added to it:
linters: linters_with_defaults(
    object_length_linter = NULL,
    object_name_linter = NULL)

title: repo
text: The repo subcommand is used to set up repositories.

title: repo
text:
Commands
  repo readme
  repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
  repo action <action-name>
  repo install repos

title: repo
text:
repo readme
This command interacts with the user to scaffold a standardized README.md for a project repository.
When executed, it prompts for the following information: - The project title. - A brief description of what the repository does. - The full names and email addresses of two primary contacts.
It then generates a README.md using the provided inputs.

title: repo
text:
Details
The generated README.md follows a clean template containing sections for the title, purpose, contact details, links (e.g. data sources, publications), and further details (e.g. methods, timeline, team, data sources).
For example, the output might look like:
# My Project Title

This repository handles data processing for the survey data.

## Contact

For more information, please contact:
- Jane Doe:
  - jane.doe@example.com
- John Smith:
  - john.smith@example.com

## Links

- [URLs to data sources (e.g. OneDrive), GitHub repositories, publications, etc.]

## Details

[Methods, timeline, team, data sources, software/tools, etc.]

title: repo
text:
repo devcontainer
This command copies a reference .devcontainer configuration into your current repository.
setupmjr repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]

--repo: Specifies the source repository and branch to copy the .devcontainer directory from (defaults to MiguelRodo/comp@main).
--build: If provided, the command will also download the relevant GitHub Action to automatically prebuild the devcontainer, fetching good default settings from the reference actions.

title: repo
text:
Details
Under the hood, the command fetches the .devcontainer directory by downloading the tarball of the specified branch from GitHub. If the --build flag is passed, it pulls the prebuild-devcontainer.yml workflow from MiguelRodo/actions and places it in .github/workflows/.

title: repo
text:
repo install repos
While setupmjr has a few subcommands like repo, the repos command is actually a dependency of setupmjr. The setupmjr repo install repos command downloads and installs this external repos utility into ~/.local/bin.
The core operations for managing repositories (cloning, configuring workspaces, etc.) are conceptually part of repos, which setupmjr uses or exposes.

title: repo
text:
repo action
This command simplifies adding pre-configured GitHub Actions to your repository.
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
It downloads the specified action workflow from the MiguelRodo/actions repository into your .github/workflows/ directory.

Available Actions
The following actions can be added:

prebuild-devcontainer: Builds and pushes a pre-built Dev Container image to GHCR whenever a SemVer tag is pushed. Read more here.
publish-quarto-site: Renders and publishes a Quarto site to the gh-pages branch whenever the main branch is updated. Read more here.
sync-issues-to-project: Syncs open issues from the repository to a GitHub Project (V2) board automatically. Read more here.
version-release: Bumps versions in Python or R packages, creates a versioned git tag, and publishes a GitHub Release. Read more here.

title: repo
text:
Details
When running repo action <action-name>, the CLI fetches the corresponding YAML file from the examples directory of the MiguelRodo/actions repository, directly placing it in .github/workflows/.

title: Installation
text: setupmjr is distributed as a compiled Go CLI binary. Install it via system package managers, release installers, or from source. Optional R and Python wrappers dispatch to the installed setupmjr binary.

title: Installation
text:
Release asset matrix
GitHub Releases publish Go CLI binaries for:

Linux (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
macOS (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
Windows (amd64, arm64) as .zip (plus .exe bare binaries for installer scripts)
Stable direct-download bare binaries for installer scripts:

setupmjr_linux_<arch>
setupmjr_darwin_<arch>
setupmjr_windows_<arch>.exe


Python and R components are wrappers around the same CLI and are platform-neutral. Install the wrapper package (pip/R) and ensure setupmjr is installed on PATH.

title: Installation
text:
Ubuntu / Debian

Option 1: Local Release Installer (No sudo required)
Install the latest release binary into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
The installer also automatically downloads the repos tool as a bundled dependency. If no writable path entry exists, the installer will stop with guidance.
To uninstall:
bash uninstall-local.sh


Option 2: Install from APT Repository (Recommended for automatic updates, but requires sudo)






Warning



The APT repository is an upcoming feature and not yet fully configured.


Install and keep setupmjr up to date directly via apt:
# Install prerequisites
sudo apt-get install -y curl gpg

# Add repository signing key
curl -fsSL https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo/KEY.gpg \
   | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg

# Add apt source
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg] https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo stable main" \
   | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/apt-miguelrodo.list >/dev/null

# Install setupmjr
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y setupmjr
To uninstall:
sudo apt-get remove setupmjr


Option 3: System-wide from Release .deb (requires sudo)
Prefer Option 1 (APT) for automatic updates. If needed, manually download and install a release .deb from the Releases page:
VERSION_SETUPMJR=1.2.6
ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"
wget "https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/releases/download/v${VERSION_SETUPMJR}/setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
sudo dpkg -i "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
rm "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"

# Fix any dependency issues
sudo apt-get install -f
To uninstall:
sudo dpkg -r setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
macOS (Homebrew)






Warning



The Homebrew tap is an upcoming feature and not yet fully configured.


brew tap MiguelRodo/setupmjr
brew install setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
Windows

Option 1: Installer Script
Download and install the pre-compiled setupmjr.exe into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:

Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
Run the installer:
.\install.ps1

The installer downloads the latest setupmjr.exe binary from GitHub releases and places it in the first writable directory in your current PATH. It also automatically downloads the repos tool as a bundled dependency.
Requirements: PowerShell and network access to GitHub releases.
(Note: Ensure you are executing this within a PowerShell console pwsh or powershell.exe, as native cmd.exe will not interpret the script correctly.)
To uninstall:
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall


Option 2: Scoop
scoop bucket add setupmjr https://github.com/MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket
scoop install setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
From Source (Go)
Requires the Go toolchain installed.
Install directly from the remote module path:
go install github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/cmd/setupmjr@latest
Or build from a local clone (Linux-specific example shown):
git clone [https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git)
cd setupmjr
go build -o setupmjr ./cmd/setupmjr
# Install system-wide on Linux/macOS
sudo mv setupmjr /usr/local/bin/

title: Installation
text:
Language Wrappers






Warning



The language wrappers are not created yet.



R Package
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("MiguelRodo/setupmjr")
Requires setupmjr on your system PATH for full wrapper coverage.


Python Package
pip install git+https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
Or from a local clone:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
pip install .
Requires setupmjr on your system PATH for full wrapper coverage.

title: Installation
text:
Verify Installation
setupmjr --help

title: hpc
text: The hpc subcommand is used to configure HPC environments.

title: hpc
text:
Commands
  hpc       Master HPC setup
  hpc git
  hpc scratch
  hpc apptainer
  hpc slurm
  hpc r

title: hpc
text:
Installation
Assuming that the HPC is running on Linux, the following line will install setupmjr without requiring sudo permission:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/main/install-local.sh | bash
Confirm that installation worked by running:
setupmjr --version
If the above does not work, then setupmjr may not be on your system PATH. In that case, you can add the following line to your shell profile (typically ~/.bashrc):
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
Then run:
source ~/.bashrc
At this point, the following should succeed:
setupmjr --version
If not, then the initial installation failed.

title: hpc
text:
Setup
The following command will configure the HPC environment:
setupmjr hpc
Apart from needing to edit one file for Git authentication if this has not been setup yet (see below), this command requires no other user input.
setupmjr hpc does the following:

Helps store large files effectively: Large files are stored in the /scratch space (if available) rather than /home, to respect HPC storage policies.
Authenticates with Git: Scripts are added to which the user needs to simply add their GitHub username and a personal access token (PAT) to enable seamless Git operations from the HPC environment.
Add Apptainer and SLURM helpers: If these tools are available on the HPC, helper scripts will be added to simplify their usage.
Configures radian: If you use radian as your R terminal, it is configured to work properly on the HPC.

Each of these features can be configured independently via the respective subcommands (hpc scratch, hpc apptainer, hpc slurm, hpc git, hpc r).

Setting up Git
To configure Git, run the following command (which is also part of the setupmjr hpc command):
setupmjr hpc git
This command simply calls setupmjr git, which configures your Git profile (name and email) via setupmjr git profile and sets up authentication credentials via setupmjr git auth.
For full details on how this works and how it configures your environment (including setting up .bashrc.d and .zshrc.d files for seamless GitHub authentication), please refer to the git setup documentation.


Using scratch space
HPCs typically have a separate scratch space for storing large files (i.e. /scratch/$USER), which is often faster and has different quotas than the home directory. The setupmjr hpc scratch command helps you configure your environment to use this scratch space effectively.
To set this up, run the following command (also part of setupmjr hpc):
setupmjr hpc scratch
This configures your environment to preferentially use the /scratch space for the following:

Apptainer and Singularity images

Automatically cached in /scratch/$USER/.cache/<apptainer/singularity> instead of the default location in the home directory.

R libraries:

The R_LIBS_USER environment variable is set to /scratch/$USER/.local/lib/R and created, so that R packages are installed in the scratch space instead of the home directory.
Similarly, various RENV_* environment variables configuring renv paths are set to point to the scratch space.

title: hpc
text:
Details
The hpc scratch command configures the environment to use the /scratch directory by doing the following:

It ensures that .bashrc.d files are sourced by .bashrc.
A script is added to ~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh, which explicitly exports paths for Apptainer, Singularity, renv, and R libraries to use /scratch/$USER. Specifically, it sets the following environment variables:

RENV_CONFIG_PAK_ENABLED=false
RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=false
RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library
RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/scratch/${USER}/renv/cache:/renv/cache
RENV_PATHS_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library
R_LIBS=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R

title: hpc
text:
Details
The hpc slurm command sets up these tools by doing the following:

It ensures that ~/.local/bin is added to your system’s PATH environment variable by (if required) adding an export statement to your .bashrc.
It places the specific utility wrapper scripts (slurm-sbatch, slurm-sintx, slurm-squeue) directly into ~/.local/bin/.

title: hpc
text:
Details
The hpc apptainer command sets up these tools by doing the following:

It ensures that ~/.local/bin is added to your system’s PATH environment variable by (if required) adding an export statement to your .bashrc.
It places the specific utility wrapper scripts directly into ~/.local/bin/.

title: multirepo
text: The multirepo subcommand acts as a wrapper around the bundled repos utility, which is installed alongside setupmjr. It is designed to manage local workspaces and batch-process actions across multiple repositories.

title: multirepo
text:
Commands
  multirepo clone
  multirepo workspace
  multirepo codespace
  multirepo create
  multirepo <other repos command>
Any command passed to setupmjr multirepo will be automatically proxied to the bundled repos tool.

title: multirepo
text:
Details
The core operations for managing multiple repositories collectively (e.g. cloning a list of repositories, configuring cross-repo VS Code workspaces) are powered by the repos utility. The multirepo subcommand simplifies their execution from the setupmjr CLI.

title: git
text: The git subcommand is used to set up git.

title: git
text:
Commands
  git
  git profile
  git auth
  git auth text
  git auth cache
  git auth mngr

title: git
text:
Setting up Git
To work with Git, you need to do two things:

Supply Git with your name and email (if not already configured).
Provide Git with credentials to authenticate with remote repositories, e.g. GitHub.

To set this up, run the following command (which is also part of the setupmjr hpc command):
setupmjr git
You will be prompted to enter your full name and email address (if these are not already set), which Git uses to identify you as the author of commits.
In addition, you will be prompted to enter your GitHub username and a personal access token (PAT). This allows Git to authenticate with GitHub when you push commits or perform other operations that require authentication.
To get a GitHub PAT, go to your GitHub account settings, navigate to “Developer settings” > “Personal access tokens”, and generate a new token with the appropriate scopes (e.g. repo for full control of private repositories).
If you skip entering any of the above information, you can always run setupmjr git again to set it up later.

title: git
text:
Details
Git authentication is configured by the following:

It is ensured that .bashrc.d and .zshrc.d files are sourced by .bashrc and .zshrc, respectively.
The credential helper is set to the following for GitHub:
!f() { sleep 1; echo "username=${GITHUB_USER:-TOKEN}"; echo "password=${GH_TOKEN:-$GITHUB_TOKEN}"; }; f
A script is added to ~/.bashrc.d/login.sh and ~/.zshrc.d/login.sh, which has space for the user to add their GitHub username and PAT, and then exports these as environment variables (GITHUB_USER and GITHUB_USERNAME for the user name and GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_PAT for the token).

title: shell
text: The shell subcommand is used to set up shell environments like bash or zsh. The bash subcommand acts as a shorthand for shell bash.

title: shell
text:
Commands
  shell <shell> rc.d
  shell <shell> path
  shell <shell> login

shell <shell> rc.d
To manage shell configuration more effectively, it is helpful to place individual scripts inside a dedicated directory (i.e. ~/.<shell>rc.d/) rather than cluttering the main ~/.<shell>rc file. The shell <shell> rc.d command sets up this directory and configures your ~/.<shell>rc to source all scripts inside it.
To set this up, run the following command:
setupmjr shell <shell> rc.d

title: shell
text:
Details
The shell <shell> rc.d command configures the environment by doing the following:

It ensures the ~/.<shell>rc.d directory exists.
It appends a loop to your ~/.<shell>rc to automatically source any readable scripts inside ~/.<shell>rc.d/:
for i in $HOME/.<shell>rc.d/*; do [ -r "$i" ] && source "$i"; done

title: shell
text:
Details
The shell <shell> path command ensures ~/bin and ~/.local/bin are accessible by doing the following:

It calls shell <shell> rc.d to ensure the ~/.<shell>rc.d/ directory is properly set up and sourced by ~/.<shell>rc.
It copies an embedded script, path-executables.sh, to ~/.<shell>rc.d/path-executables.sh. This script safely appends ~/bin and ~/.local/bin to the PATH environment variable if they are not already included.
